scimon.text: Which method can be used for reduce the sintering temperature, and why?

hidden_target.material_initial_state: Homogeneous gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder, sieved to 10–60 μm, dispersed in an acrylate-based photocurable resin to form a slurry and DLP-printed into layered green bodies.
hidden_target.intervention: The DLP-printed green bodies were debound under either oxygen-rich ambient air or an oxygen-deficient environment maintained by continuous mechanical-pump evacuation, then solid-state sintered at 800, 1000, 1050, or 1100 °C for 24 h. Debinding included 1 h holds at 300 and 450 °C followed by heating to 500 °C.
hidden_target.conditions: Specimens were printed with a 405 nm source at 19.57 mW/cm², 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, and 20 layers, then ultrasonically cleaned in ethanol. Atmosphere-dependent debinding and subsequent furnace sintering were compared over 800–1100 °C; a 600 °C sample disintegrated and was excluded from the main sintering analysis.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: Oxygen-deficient debinding retained carbon in former resin regions, reduced pore volume, limited cracking, and permitted earlier loss of the layered morphology and stronger interparticle bonding. Oxygen-rich debinding produced higher oxygen content and particle-surface oxide layers, more porous/cracked structures, and delayed elimination of particle and layer boundaries.
hidden_target.mechanism: In oxygen-rich debinding, oxidation of resin and powder generates rapidly escaping CO/CO2, causing pressure-driven surface cracking; surface oxides subsequently resist interparticle mass transport and delay densification, although an Al-rich oxide layer can protect against further oxidation. With deficient oxygen, incomplete carbon oxidation leaves residual carbon, diminishes gas evolution and porosity, and facilitates diffusion, interfacial bonding, and load transfer at lower sintering temperatures. At elevated temperature, thermally activated elemental interdiffusion progressively consolidates the powder particles.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to oxygen-rich debinding, oxygen-deficient debinding is reported to produce earlier densification and comparable maximum compressive strength at a 50 °C lower sintering temperature, while reducing debinding-induced surface cracking.
hidden_target.baseline: DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi specimens debound in oxygen-rich ambient air and sintered for 24 h; these required 1100 °C for full consolidation and approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength.
hidden_target.boundary: The result applies to the studied DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi powder/resin system and the specified debinding schedule, atmospheres, and 24 h sintering treatments. Below about 1000 °C elemental diffusion remained limited, while at 1100 °C oxygen-deficient samples developed stripe-like precipitates attributed to localized softening or melting of fine particles without oxide protection.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: SEM of top, side, and polished cross-sectional surfaces was used to assess cracks, porosity, particle interfaces, layered morphology, and consolidation; EDS mapping quantified carbon, oxygen, aluminum, nickel, and interfacial redistribution; compression testing with an MTS universal testing machine measured strength versus atmosphere and sintering temperature.
hidden_target.actual_result: After debinding, oxygen-rich samples contained 9.3 at.% O and 21.7 at.% residual C and exhibited gas-induced surface cracking, whereas oxygen-deficient samples contained 3.7 at.% O and 33.6 at.% C and showed no surface cracks. The layered structure disappeared at 1100 °C under oxygen-rich conditions but at 1050 °C under oxygen-deficient conditions. Oxygen-rich specimens increased from about 0.5 MPa at 800 °C to 5.17 MPa at 1100 °C. Oxygen-deficient specimens increased from about 2.4 MPa at 800 °C to 4.93 MPa at 1050 °C and only about 5.1 MPa at 1100 °C, demonstrating comparable strength and near-saturated consolidation at 1050 °C, 50 °C below the oxygen-rich requirement.
